title: Monday.com vs Plane
comparison_markdown:
# Monday.com vs Plane (2026)

## Overview
Monday.com is a proprietary, cloud-based work OS designed for cross-functional team collaboration, resource management, and visual project tracking. Plane is an open-source, issue-tracking and project management tool built specifically for software engineering teams seeking a modular, developer-centric alternative to Jira and proprietary trackers. Engineering leaders and operations managers evaluate these platforms to balance ease-of-use against data ownership, extensibility, and infrastructure costs.

## Key Differences
* **Cost:** Monday.com operates on a tiered SaaS subscription model ranging from $9 to $19+ per user per month, whereas Plane is free and open-source for self-hosted deployments with optional paid cloud tiers.
* **Data Ownership:** Monday.com stores all organizational data within its managed proprietary cloud infrastructure, while Plane allows complete self-hosting via Docker for full data sovereignty and compliance control.
* **Setup Complexity:** Monday.com offers immediate out-of-the-box deployment via web browsers with guided onboarding, whereas Plane requires technical administration to provision, secure, and maintain server infrastructure.
* **Scalability:** Monday.com scales through enterprise SaaS tiers with centralized IT controls, whereas Plane scales horizontally via container orchestration based on the capacity of the underlying host infrastructure.
* **Feature Integration:** Monday.com relies on native app marketplace connectors and built-in automation recipes for CRM and marketing tools, whereas Plane focuses tightly on GitHub/GitLab integrations, cycles, and modular issue hierarchies.

## Pricing Comparison
| Aspect | Monday.com | Plane |
|--------|----------|---------|
| Base Cost | $9-$19/user/month | Free (self-hosted) |
| License | Proprietary | Apache 2.0 |
| Self-hosting | Not available | Available |
| Per-user cost at 50 users | ~$450-$950/month (Standard/Pro tiers) | $0 (server cost only) |
| Per-user cost at 200 users | ~$1,800-$3,800+/month (Pro/Enterprise tiers) | $0 (server cost only) |

## Pros and Cons

### Monday.com
* **Pros:**
  * Intuitive, highly customizable visual dashboards and board views
  * Extensive native integrations with major enterprise software suites
  * Zero infrastructure maintenance or self-hosting overhead
  * Robust built-in time tracking and resource management capabilities
* **Cons:**
  * High cumulative software costs that scale linearly with headcount
  * Strict vendor lock-in with proprietary data formats
  * Feature bloat for teams that only require software issue tracking
  * Complex permission management on lower-tier plans

### Plane
* **Pros:**
  * Permissive Apache 2.0 open-source license with no user license fees
  * Complete data ownership via Docker-based self-hosting
  * Clean, fast, developer-centric interface optimized for speed
  * Native git provider integrations (GitHub, GitLab) out of the box
* **Cons:**
  * Requires dedicated DevOps resources for maintenance, backups, and updates
  * Smaller ecosystem of third-party plugins compared to established SaaS tools
  * Lacks advanced native CRM, marketing portfolio, and financial budgeting views
  * Documentation for complex enterprise configurations is still maturing

## When to Choose Each
Choose Monday.com if you manage cross-functional business operations, marketing, sales pipelines, and creative teams that require a centralized, no-code visual workspace without internal IT maintenance. It is best suited for organizations of any size that prioritize out-of-the-box integrations, user-friendly onboarding, and guaranteed cloud uptime over infrastructure control.

Choose Plane if you run software engineering, product development, or technical teams that need a fast, keyboard-first issue tracker with robust cycle planning and git synchronization. It is ideal for startups, tech companies, and privacy-conscious organizations that want to eliminate per-seat SaaS licensing costs and maintain strict control over their source code and project data on their own infrastructure.

## Migration Path
1. Export existing tasks, statuses, and metadata from Monday.com boards into CSV format using the platform's native export utility.
2. Provision a production-ready server environment and deploy Plane using Docker Compose according to the official documentation.
3. Map Monday.com columns, priorities, and custom fields to Plane's schema architecture (modules, cycles, and states).
4. Import the structured data into Plane using available community migration scripts or REST API bulk import routines.
5. Configure webhooks and connect git repositories (GitHub or GitLab) to re-establish code-to-issue traceability.

## Our Take
Plane is production-ready for agile engineering teams comfortable with Docker-based deployments, offering a clean and responsive interface that rivals proprietary alternatives. However, potential adopters must account for a significant technical limitation: Plane lacks the sprawling no-code automation engine and massive marketplace integrations found in mature enterprise platforms, meaning custom workflows often require direct API scripting. 

Organizations heavily reliant on cross-functional business operations, CRM pipelines, and non-technical stakeholder reporting should remain on Monday.com. Conversely, software-driven teams looking to slash per-seat subscription fees while retaining absolute data sovereignty should transition to Plane immediately, provided they possess the internal system administration bandwidth to manage self-hosted infrastructure.

## Who Should Switch
* Engineering teams of 25-100 developers who do not need advanced marketing portfolio management or resource utilization heatmaps.
* Open-source projects and privacy-focused startups that do not want third-party SaaS vendors storing their proprietary product roadmaps.
* Cost-conscious organizations with dedicated infrastructure engineers who do not want to pay per-user software license fees scaling past $3,000 monthly.
* Development squads that prioritize keyboard shortcuts, cycle planning, and deep git integrations over generic spreadsheet-style project grids.
* IT departments under strict compliance mandates that prohibit storing internal task data on external, third-party cloud servers.

## FAQ

### Can Plane completely replace Monday.com for non-technical teams?
No. While Plane excels at software issue tracking and cycle management, it lacks the broad no-code workspace flexibility, CRM capabilities, and financial tracking features that marketing and sales teams rely on in Monday.com.

### Is there an official automated migration tool from Monday.com to Plane?
No direct, one-click automated importer built into the core UI currently exists for Monday.com to Plane. Migrations typically require exporting data to CSV and utilizing custom scripts or API integrations to map fields.

### Does Plane offer a managed cloud option for teams that do not want to self-host?
Yes, Plane offers hosted cloud subscription tiers for teams that prefer a turnkey SaaS experience without managing their own Docker containers or server infrastructure.

### How does Plane handle user permissions compared to Monday.com?
Plane utilizes a more streamlined, workspace-and-project-level access control model tailored for software teams. Monday.com provides granular, column- and item-level permission controls that are better suited for mixed corporate hierarchies on Enterprise plans.

### Are git integrations free on Plane?
Yes, integrations with platforms like GitHub and GitLab are included out of the box in the open-source self-hosted version of Plane at no additional cost.
meta_description: Plane offers a free, self-hosted open-source alternative to Monday.com for engineering teams. See full comparison.
